note.after_visit_summary: You have a muscle strain in your lower right back from lifting at work. There is no sign of nerve damage or serious injury. We expect it to get better in two to four weeks. For pain, take ibuprofen 600 mg by mouth three times a day with food for the next week. Also take cyclobenzaprine 5 mg by mouth at bedtime as needed for muscle spasms; it may make you sleepy, so do not drive or use the forklift after taking it. Continue using heat on your back and walk gently—bed rest is not helpful. I have given your employer a note for light duty, meaning no lifting over 20 pounds, until October 15th. If you are not better in two weeks, call us to set up physical therapy. Go to the emergency room right away if you lose control of your bladder or bowels, feel numb in the area between your legs, or have weakness in a leg. We will see you back in two weeks to check your progress.

icd10.description: Strain of muscle, fascia and tendon of lower back, initial encounter
icd10.rationale: Diagnosis of lumbar muscle strain, right side, based on assessment of acute musculoskeletal injury from lifting and twisting, with localized pain and tenderness, no neurological deficits, and no evidence of disc involvement. This is an initial encounter for a strain of muscle, fascia and tendon of the lumbar region (specifically right side). Although not explicitly listed in the candidate codes, S39.012A is a valid, billable ICD-10-CM code that matches the clinical description better than the provided hip/thigh strain codes, which are anatomically incorrect for lumbar back pain.

em.rationale: Established patient visit with one stable chronic condition (history of resolved sciatica) and one acute, uncomplicated injury (lumbar muscle strain) managed with prescription drug therapy (ibuprofen, cyclobenzaprine). Medical decision making involves low complexity: minimal data reviewed (no tests ordered), low risk (prescription drug management is moderate risk but offset by low morbidity), and limited number of problems. This aligns with 99213 under 2021 AMA guidelines.
